precepts.why:

Jump to the end of the chapter: “For they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor”. They vex you with their wiles, their seduction, and beguiled you into worshipping their gods. They knew: we have to get these people to sin against their God. “For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world”. It was Moab then, and it is all the nations now. Today the majority of the pornography is controlled by Amalek and Edom. They understood: we are going to destroy the minds of the people. We are not the only race having sex, but all our music is derogatory and evil, every video is a twerk video, and even somebody’s grandmother is twerking online. Everything is over-sexualized to destroy the minds of our young people, along with the drugs, the whoring and the music.

These are the wiles of the devil. The Lord would not let Balaam curse Israel, so the counsel was to make Israel fall through whoredom. As long as we continue in whoredom we will not build healthy marriages, we will not produce spiritually healthy children, and the generational curses keep going. precepts.text: These caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor.
precepts.point: They called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat and bowed down; Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled. The worship of Baal-peor went into whoredom, that orgy worship: we started worshipping another god and messing with the women together.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

precepts.why:
Israel abode in Shittim, “and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab.” Why? Balaam could not curse us, because God said you cannot curse what is blessed; so his counsel was the best the enemy can ever do: throw another god in front of Israel and send the women, and let Israel bring the trespass on himself.

Moses names it after the war with Midian: “Have ye saved all the women alive? Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.”

The daughters that called Israel to the sacrifices of their gods were sent by the counsel of Balaam. That counsel is why the Lord put Balaam to death. The worship of Baal-peor went into whoredom, that orgy worship: we started worshipping another god and messing with the women together, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.

precepts.text: The times of this ignorance God winked at, but now commandeth all men every where to repent, for He hath appointed a day of judgment by Christ.
precepts.point: Do not take that mercy lightly, and do not frustrate the grace of God until He is finished with you. He can cut a man's days down whenever He wants; do not press Him to it.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

precepts.why:
The Lord said, “Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun”, and Moses said to the judges, “Slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baal–peor”: every judge by his rank, the officer over ten took ten, the officer over fifty took fifty, and so on. With the Most High it is two options only, life and death. Under the old covenant there was no winking at ignorance; judgment was instant.

The only reason we are not judged that way now for the gods we served is the grace and mercy given through Christ. “Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man’s device. And the times of this ignorance God winked at; but now commandeth all men every where to repent.” The times of this ignorance He winked at: the Christianity with the white Jesus, the Islam, the Buddhism, the Hinduism, the Egyptology, the atheism.

But now He commandeth all men every where to repent, “Because he hath appointed a day, in the which he will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom he hath ordained; whereof he hath given assurance unto all men, in that he hath raised him from the dead.” That man is Jesus the Christ.

Do not take that mercy lightly, and do not frustrate the grace of God until He is finished with you. He can cut a man's days down whenever He wants; do not press Him to it.

precepts.point: These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play, and that play means sex; that was the golden calf. Neither commit fornication as they did, when three and twenty thousand fell in one day; neither tempt Christ, for it was Christ with us in the wilderness. These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

precepts.why:
Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, rose up from among the congregation with a javelin and thrust the man of Israel and the Midianitish woman through, and the plague was stayed. He is written in the register of famous men.

“Let us now praise famous men, and our fathers that begat us.” This is the record in which Phinehas is honored, one of the fathers that begat us, praised for what he did in the sight of Moses and all the congregation.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

precepts.why:
While the whole congregation wept before the door of the tabernacle, one man brought a Midianitish woman to his brethren in the sight of all: a man that did not care about his people while everyone around him mourned. Phinehas saw it and rose up.

“The third in glory is Phinees the son of Eleazar, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord, and stood up with good courage of heart: when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel.” Phinehas stands third in glory, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord and stood up with good courage of heart when the people were turned back, and made reconciliation for Israel.

“Therefore was there a covenant of peace made with him, that he should be the chief of the sanctuary and of his people, and that he and his posterity should have the dignity of the priesthood for ever.” The javelin that stayed the plague from the children of Israel won him the covenant of peace and the priesthood for ever.

precepts.why:
Those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand, and Paul tells us why it is written. “Now these things were our examples, to the intent we should not lust after evil things, as they also lusted.”

“Neither be ye idolaters, as were some of them; as it is written, The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.” That play means sex; that was the golden calf. “Neither let us commit fornication, as some of them committed, and fell in one day three and twenty thousand.” That is Baal-peor and the daughters of Moab. “Neither let us tempt Christ, as some of them also tempted, and were destroyed of serpents”: it was Christ with us in the wilderness.

“Now all these things happened unto them for ensamples: and they are written for our admonition, upon whom the ends of the world are come.” These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

precepts.why:
Phinehas received the covenant of peace and the everlasting priesthood “because he was zealous for his God, and made an atonement for the children of Israel.” Being zealous today is confessing Christ before men, and you confess him mainly through your actions.

“For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps.” Christ suffered for us and left us an example that we should follow his steps, and his steps were keeping the commandments of God.

The first way you deny Christ is by rejecting the commandments. We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

The covenant of peace given to Phinehas is what all of us are striving for, rest from this servitude of bondage, but you must be zealous for the law of the Most High to obtain it, and that zeal costs something. “Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.”

“He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.” Phinehas thrust through a man of Israel in the sight of the congregation; that is zeal that lets nothing of the household come first.

We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

Be zealous for the law and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers. That covenant of peace, rest from this servitude of bondage, is what all of us are striving for, and zeal for the law is how it is obtained.

precepts.text: The people began whoredom with the daughters of Moab and were joined unto Baal-peor; that history is the reason the Lord commanded the vengeance.
precepts.point: The Most High told Israel to avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites. The reason for this vengeance is the history of Numbers 25; go back and read that chapter to see what Midian did.

note.label: Numbers 31: Vengeance on the Midianites

precepts.why:
“Avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites.” The reason for this vengeance is the history of Numbers 25. “And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods.”

“And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.” The whoredom with the daughters of the other nations and the joining unto Baal-peor is what Midian did to Israel, and it is why the Lord commanded Moses to avenge the children of Israel before he was gathered unto his people.

precepts.text: Phinehas took a javelin and thrust the man of Israel and the Midianitish woman through, and the plague was stayed.
precepts.point: Phinehas is the one who killed the man of Israel that was fornicating with the woman of the other nation, in the history of Numbers 25.

note.label: Numbers 31: Vengeance on the Midianites

precepts.why:
Twelve thousand armed for war, a thousand of every tribe, went to the war with “Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest”, with the holy instruments and the trumpets to blow in his hand. Phinehas is the one who killed the man of Israel that was fornicating with the woman of the other nation in the history of Numbers 25.

“And when Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, and took a javelin in his hand; And he went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.”

The priest who stayed the plague with a javelin is the priest sent with the army to avenge the Lord of Midian.

precepts.text: Those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand; that plague in the matter of Peor is why the women who had known man could not be kept.
precepts.point: Moses allowed the men to keep those women so they would not commit sin and go raping the women, being out at war. That does not mean it is done today; it was a time that the Most High allowed it so the men would not be in the midst of sin.

note.label: Numbers 31: Vengeance on the Midianites

precepts.why:
Moses was wroth with the officers of the host because they saved all the women alive. “Behold, these caused the children of Israel, through the counsel of Balaam, to commit trespass against the Lord in the matter of Peor, and there was a plague among the congregation of the Lord.” Balaam took it upon himself to send the women of the other nations to Israel, and it caused the people to go into fornication, and the Lord began putting them to death.

“And those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.” That plague in the matter of Peor is why every woman that had known man by lying with him could not be kept, and every male among the little ones was killed.

The women children that had not known a man they kept alive for themselves. Moses allowed the men to keep those women so they would not commit sin and go raping the women, being out at war. That does not mean it is done today; it was a time that the Most High allowed it so the men would not be in the midst of sin.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

precepts.why:
Israel sent Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest with ten princes to Gilead. When you send Phinehas it is a problem, because of the kind of man Phinehas was: where he showed up, the zeal of the Most High showed up with him. It goes back to Baalpeor. “And Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. And they called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods: and the people did eat, and bowed down to their gods. And Israel joined himself unto Baal–peor: and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.”

The men of Israel committed whoredom with the daughters of Moab, ate of the sacrifices of their gods, bowed down to them, and joined themselves unto Baalpeor. That is what the anger of the Most High was kindled over, and that is the history behind the man they sent.

So when Phinehas showed up at Gilead, everybody knew it was about to go down.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

precepts.why:
“And the Lord said unto Moses, Take all the heads of the people, and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel. And Moses said unto the judges of Israel, Slay ye every one his men that were joined unto Baal–peor.”

The heads of the people joined to Baalpeor hanged up before the Lord against the sun: that is how the fierce anger of the Lord is turned away. This is the judgment Phinehas stood in, and why his coming to the two and a half tribes in Gilead meant business.

note.label: Joshua 22: The Altar of Witness

precepts.why:
“And, behold, one of the children of Israel came and brought unto his brethren a Midianitish woman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation of the children of Israel, who were weeping before the door of the tabernacle of the congregation.” One man of Israel was so bold he brought her to his brethren while the whole congregation wept. It was once a shameful thing for our men to be seen like that; today men and women of Israel walk boldly and proudly with the nations, that same spirit.

“And when Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, and took a javelin in his hand; And he went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel. And those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.”

That is Phinehas. So when Phinehas showed up at Gilead with the ten princes, everybody knew it was about to go down.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

At Shittim the daughters of Moab drew Israel into whoredom, and from there into the sacrifices of their gods, eating and bowing down to them. That is the history behind the law, and it is what Israel was stepping back into when the sons of Naomi took wives of Moab.

points: While the Most High God was passing judgment and the congregation was weeping before the door of the tabernacle, one of the children of Israel brought a Midianitish woman in the sight of Moses and all the congregation. No fear; all he cared about was fulfilling his lust.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin in his hand, and thrust both of them through. And those that died in the plague were 24,000. In one day God killed 24,000, because of sin.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: The people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab, and over those women they went into the sacrifices to other gods and ate the food after it was offered.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: Israel joined himself unto Baalpeor and the anger of the Lord was kindled. So what do you mean we should not keep the commandments? Telling a people not to read the Old Testament is the smartest thing you could do if you want to destroy them.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: The Lord told Moses to take all the heads of the people and hang them up, and Moses told the judges to slay every one his men that were joined to Baalpeor. That is how seriously Israel was judged — and it was Levites who carried it out.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: Israel abode in Shittim, and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab. Why? Balaam could not curse us, because God said you cannot curse what is blessed; so his counsel was the best the enemy can ever do: throw another god in front of Israel and send the women, and let Israel bring the trespass on himself. That counsel is why the Lord put Balaam to death.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

points: They called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods, and the people did eat and bowed down; Israel joined himself unto Baal-peor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled. The worship of Baal-peor went into whoredom, that orgy worship: we started worshipping another god and messing with the women together.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

points: The Lord said, take all the heads of the people and hang them up before the Lord against the sun, that His fierce anger be turned away; and Moses said unto the judges, slay ye every one his man that were joined unto Baal-peor. Every one his man means every judge by his rank: the officer over ten took ten, the officer over fifty took fifty, and so on. With the Most High it is two options only, life and death.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

points: Under the old covenant there was no winking at ignorance; judgment was instant. The only reason we are not judged that way now for the gods we served is the grace and mercy given through Christ: the times of this ignorance God winked at, the Christianity with the white Jesus, the Islam, the Buddhism, the Hinduism, the Egyptology, the atheism; but now He commandeth all men every where to repent, because He hath appointed a day in which He will judge the world in righteousness by that man whom He hath ordained, Jesus the Christ.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

points: While the whole congregation wept before the door of the tabernacle, one of the children of Israel brought a Midianitish woman unto his brethren in the sight of Moses and all the congregation: a man that did not care about his people while everyone around him mourned.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

points: When Phinehas the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin in his hand, went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through; so the plague was stayed from the children of Israel, and those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

points: These things were our examples, that we should not lust after evil things as they lusted. The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play, and that play means sex; that was the golden calf. Neither commit fornication as they did, when three and twenty thousand fell in one day; neither tempt Christ, for it was Christ with us in the wilderness. These things are written for our admonition, that we be warned: idolatry leads to whoredom, spiritual whoredom against the Most High and physical whoredom with it.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

points: Phinehas turned the wrath of the Most High away from the children of Israel, because he was zealous for his God's sake among them; wherefore the Lord gave him His covenant of peace, and to his seed after him the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he made an atonement for the children of Israel.

That covenant of peace is what all of us are striving for, rest from this servitude of bondage; but the wisdom in reading the acts of Phinehas is that you must be zealous for the law of the Most High to obtain it. Be ye zealous for the law, and give your lives for the covenant of your fathers; Phinehas our father, in being zealous and fervent, obtained the covenant of an everlasting priesthood.

Being zealous today is confessing Christ before men, and you confess him mainly through your actions. Christ suffered for us, leaving us an example that we should follow his steps, and his steps were keeping the commandments of God; the first way you deny Christ is by rejecting the commandments.

Christ came not to send peace on earth but a sword, setting a man at variance against his own household; he that loveth father or mother more than him is not worthy of him. We stay zealous by letting nothing separate us from following Christ in his steps: keeping the laws of God, teaching the gospel, and spreading the word with wisdom.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

points: The man of Israel that was slain was Zimri the son of Salu, a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites; the woman was Cozbi the daughter of Zur, head over a people of a chief house in Midian. The charge stands to Simeon to get it together; Simeon is coming back with the rest of the tribes.

note.label: Numbers 25: Baal-peor and the Zeal of Phinehas

points: The Lord said unto Moses, vex the Midianites and smite them, for they vex you with their wiles, wherewith they have beguiled you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi.
